subject: Enclave boundary narrative and diagrams for SIG review
messages:
From: Lisa Huang <lisa.huang@acme-analytics.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acme-analytics.com
Date: 2026-11-23T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: Enclave boundary narrative and diagrams for SIG review

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for taking the time on Friday. As part of Acme's SIG submission we need a concise security architecture narrative that describes how Redwood's Dedicated and Private deployments enforce tenant isolation at the network and control-plane level. Specifically we need:

- A one-page narrative describing the "enclave" boundaries (control plane vs data plane) and where customer workloads run for both Dedicated and Private deployments.
- Network diagrams with annotated traffic flows (north-south, east-west, control-plane egress) at a level we can include in the SIG packet.
- A short matrix that maps common SIG/CAIQ questions (network segmentation, egress control, private connectivity) to the evidence artifacts you can provide.

Deadlines: we are aiming to submit the SIG package next week (target 2026-12-01). Could you confirm whether you can provide drafts by end of day Tuesday (2026-11-24)? If a call helps to scope this, we can set one up tomorrow.

Thanks,
Lisa Huang
Security Program Manager
Acme Analytics
[Attachment: acme_sig_request.pdf (PDF, 220KB)]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Huang <lisa.huang@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-23T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Enclave boundary narrative and diagrams for SIG review

Hi Lisa,

Appreciate the clear ask. Kimberly and Neha are the right folks for diagrams and CAIQ mapping respectively — looping them in. We can produce: a short narrative (1 page), two diagrams (Dedicated and Private) with annotated arrows showing control-plane interactions, and a 2-tab spreadsheet mapping SIG/CAIQ items to artifacts.

Quick notes on scope so we align:
- Level of detail: we will provide network-level zones (VPC/subnet-level) and named infra components (control plane, inference pool, shared services), but we won't include low-level host IPs or customer-specific identifiers.
- Sensitive elements: KMS/HSM callouts will be included at a high level; key material details remain redacted.
- Evidence: where possible we'll attach existing SOC2/architecture artifacts (e.g., perimeter policy screenshots) and point to Drive links for larger diagrams.

We can deliver draft artifacts by EOD Tuesday (2026-11-24). If you want a short sync tomorrow at 10:00 AM PT to confirm annotation style, Kimberly and I can join.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Staff Security Architect
Redwood Inference

Thanks Mateo — that works. A couple clarifications before the sync:

1) For the Private deployment, can you explicitly call out connection patterns for customer-managed VPNs and any supported transit gateway model? We need to document how traffic enters the customer VPC and how outbound egress is controlled.
2) For Dedicated, please annotate how tenancy is enforced (dedicated GPU pools, network ACLs, NSGs) and whether any shared services (monitoring/metrics collectors) are multi-tenant.
3) For the CAIQ mapping, can you flag any items that are not yet covered by existing artifacts so we can track follow-ups?

Sync confirmed for tomorrow 10:00 AM PT. If you have a short pre-read URL that would be great; otherwise the draft PDFs/spreadsheet are fine.

Regards,
Lisa
[Acme internal note: target SIG submission 2026-12-01]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Huang <lisa.huang@acme-analytics.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-24T15:40:00-08:00
Subject: Enclave boundary narrative and diagrams (draft) — Redwood Inference

Hi Lisa — attaching the first drafts per the scope discussed. High level summary up top, followed by two diagrams (Dedicated, Private) and a CAIQ mapping spreadsheet.

Summary (bullet):
- Dedicated: customer workloads run in tenant-dedicated GPU pools inside customer-specific VPCs. Control plane remains in Redwood-managed control VPCs and communicates over authenticated mTLS channels. Shared observability collectors exist but pull telemetry from tenant pools via per-customer ingest keys — collectors do not hold customer data beyond ephemeral metrics.
- Private: when deployed in a customer VPC (VPC-hosted Private), the control plane may be customer-managed (private control plane) or Redwood-hosted across a private peering link. Traffic ingress uses customer-managed VPN or cloud direct connect; egress paths are governed by customer route tables and Redwood egress proxies as requested.
- Egress & Fencing: Automatic egress policies are available; by default Dedicated deployments restrict outbound to approved endpoints and log all egress requests.

Attachments included (stubs):
- enclave_boundary_v1.pdf (diagram PDF, 2 pages) — contains both Dedicated and Private annotated diagrams.
- traffic_pattern_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet) — rows: flow, source zone, destination, protocol, port, control-plane?
- CAIQ-mapping-draft.docx (docx) — mapping of SIG/CAIQ questions to available artifacts and outstanding asks.

Outstanding items (we flagged these in the CAIQ mapping):
- One CAIQ item (network egress retention policy for Private deployments in customer-managed control planes) needs customer-specific confirmation — we left an action for Acme to confirm desired retention window.
- A minor diagram clarification: for Private control-plane peering we have two supported modes (peer-to-peer vs. transit) — we used peer-to-peer in the draft; if Acme prefers transit gateway, we can update quickly.

Links: short read link to Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/EnclaveBoundary/enclave_boundary_v1.pdf
Jira for follow-ups: JIRA-RED-8421

Next steps:
- Please review the CAIQ mapping and mark any items you want us to expand.
- If the diagrams look good, we can produce redacted PNGs suitable for inclusion in the SIG packet.

Thanks — happy to hop on a follow-up if you want changes prior to submission.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
